title: Observation envelope
description: The universal wrapper every Epidemica observation travels in, from any module and any channel. This schema describes what a **client sends**: server-assigned fields (received_at, validated, validation_error) are deliberately absent, so `additionalProperties: false` mechanically rejects a client that tries to supply them. The `payload` is NOT validated here; the server dereferences `schema_uri` and validates it separately, which is what lets payload contracts version independently of the envelope. See docs/concepts/observation-envelope.md and ADR-0002.
$comment: Where a `format` keyword and a `pattern` overlap, the pattern is normative. JSON Schema's format vocabulary is optional and its support varies between implementations and languages -- the Elixir server, the Dart client and the Python tooling do not agree on which formats they check -- so anything that must actually be enforced is expressed as a pattern. The formats are retained as documentation and as extra strictness where a validator does support them.

envelope_version.description: Selects the envelope schema the server validates against. Additive changes publish a new minor (1.1) with its own schema file; servers accept every 1.x they know. See ADR-0007.

study_id.description: The study this observation belongs to. Epidemica observations are always study-scoped; there is no such thing as a study-less observation.

protocol_hash.description: Hash of the exact Study Protocol Bundle version in force on the device when this was recorded. This is what makes a dataset reproducible: you can always answer which version of the study produced any given row.

subject.description: Client-generated pseudonym. Never PII. The character class is a deliberate guard rather than a formatting preference: it makes an email address or any string containing '@', '.' or whitespace fail validation outright. A UUIDv4 with hyphens is the recommended value.
subject.$comment: A bare phone number would still pass this pattern; the guard reduces accidental PII, it does not eliminate it. Enforcement also lives in code review and the privacy tests.

device_id.description: Identifies one app installation, not one physical device or one person. Reinstalling produces a new device_id, which is the correct interpretation: the outbox and its seq counter are gone.

module.description: The module that produced this observation, e.g. 'proximity', 'instruments', 'reach'. Open-ended so third-party modules need no change to this contract.

schema_uri.description: Absolute, immutable, resolvable URI of the payload contract. Dereferences to a JSON Schema plus a JSON-LD context, which is how FAIR/DCAT export becomes a build step instead of a research project. https is required in production; http is tolerated for local development.

observed_at.description: When the observation happened, by the device clock. Must be UTC with a 'Z' suffix -- mixed UTC offsets across a multi-site study are a recurring data-quality failure, so they are rejected at the contract rather than cleaned up in analysis.

clock_offset_ms.description: Device clock minus reference clock, in milliseconds, as measured against NTP or the server. Required but nullable: null means 'not measured', which analysis must distinguish from a verified zero. Never substitute 0 for unknown.

seq.description: Monotonic counter per device install, allocated in the same transaction as the outbox insert. With device_id it forms the idempotency key. It does NOT reset per study, so a device in two studies produces one interleaved stream: max(seq) is not a per-study observation count, and within-study gaps are expected. Count rows; never infer counts from seq.
seq.$comment: The first value a device allocates may be 0 or 1, and nothing may assume which. The reference client's outbox is a SQLite AUTOINCREMENT column, whose first row is 1; the minimum here is a bound on the field, not a declaration of where a stream starts.

payload.description: Module-specific content, validated separately against schema_uri. Binary attachments (photos, audio) are uploaded out of band and referenced here; they are never inlined as base64.
